courses.title: Agriculture: The Foundation of Civilizations
courses.description: [GE 3B] Introduction to the genesis and evolution of agriculture as the foundation of civilizations throughout history. Analyzing agriculture within the context of the development and evolution of various civilizations over time. Emphasis on critical analysis of the historical development of agriculture in various parts of the world including the United States using documentary and literature collections. Open to all majors. Required of all College of Agriculture majors.

courses.title: Ethical Issues in Food, Agricultural and Apparel Industries
courses.description: [GE 3C or 4C] Socioeconomic and scientific issues in the Food, Agricultural, and Apparel Systems within a framework of moral philosophy and ethical reasoning. Analysis of topics in biotechnology in agricultural and apparel production, food processing, intellectual property rights, food safety, nutrition, the treatment of animals, the environment, labor rights in a global marketplace, and reducing world hunger and malnutrition.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Parasitology and Infectious Diseases
courses.description: Animal parasites and pathogens and their relationship to clinical and subclinical parasitic diseases, as well as common diseases and disease processes of livestock, companion animals, laboratory animals and wildlife. Per university policy, students must receive a C- (1.7) or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 3305L .
courses.prerequisites: AHS major, AVS major, AG Science major, AG 1010 , or instructor permission; BIO 1150 or BIO 1210 ; and BIO 1150L or BIO 1210L .

courses.title: Parasitology and Infectious Diseases Laboratory
courses.description: Study of animal parasites and pathogens and their relationship to clinical and subclinical parasitic diseases, as well as common diseases and disease processes of livestock, companion animals, laboratory animals and wildlife. Per department policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): AHS 3305 .
courses.prerequisites: AHS major, AVS major, AG Science major, AG 1010 , or instructor permission; BIO 1150 or BIO 1210 ; and BIO 1150L or BIO 1210L .

courses.title: Basic Microbiology
courses.description: A study of cell structure, function, metabolism, genetics, and diversity of microorganisms. The impacts of microorganisms on evolutionary, environmental and disease processes are discussed. Corequisite(s): BIO 2060L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Basic Microbiology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory techniques and methods used to study of cell structure, function, metabolism, genetics, and diversity of microorganisms. Identification and growth of microorganisms, as well as scientific thinking, are emphasized in the laboratory exercises. Corequisite(s): BIO 2060 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Orientation to Animal and Veterinary Sciences
courses.description: Outlining the academic path that students will follow to be successful in this major. Discuss the various employment opportunities available for students graduating with this degree. Covering campus life, university rules, policies and regulations. Mandatory fall quarter course for entering freshmen. Strategies to assist students with the transition from school to university and the successful completion of their college career in the Animal & Veterinary Science department. Topics covered include: campus student support services, career planning, time management, academic planning, study/note/test skills, learning styles, navigating the college and university, professional development, extracurricular activities, and others.
courses.prerequisites: AVS major.

courses.title: Food Animal Production
courses.description: A study of the domestic livestock industry and animal management techniques emphasizing the importance of management strategies, equipment and facilities, nutrition, selection, breeding principles and disease control to ensure scientifically based management decisions.
courses.prerequisites: AVS major.

courses.title: Companion, Laboratory and Exotic Animal Care
courses.description: General concepts of handling and restraining domestic and exotic animals. Emphasis will be placed on behavior, management, nutrition, disease prevention, and breed identification. The care and use of laboratory animals will be covered in depth.
courses.prerequisites: AVS major.

courses.title: Food Animal Production Laboratory
courses.description: A study of the commonly applied animal techniques and practices used to scientifically manage livestock in the commercial food animal industry. The laboratory will emphasize the importance of evaluating business management strategies, equipment and facilities, nutrition, genetics and selection, breeding principles and herd health plans in order of evaluate scientifically based domestic animal livestock management methodologies. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: AVS major.

courses.title: Companion Animal Management Laboratory
courses.description: Instruction will cover the general concepts of handling and restraining domestic and exotic animals. Emphasis will be placed on behavior, management, nutrition, disease prevention, and breed identification. The care and use of laboratory animals will be covered in depth. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: AVS major.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Animal Nutrition
courses.description: A comprehensive introduction to animal nutrition with an emphasis on nutrients, digestive physiology, digestion, and feedstuff characteristics. Focus on developing a foundation for understanding more advanced topics in nutrition including the interaction between health and nutrition. Corequisite(s): AVS 2101L .
courses.prerequisites: AVS 1112 ; CHM 1210 ; CHM 1210L ; MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , or MAT 1140 ; and AVS major.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Animal Nutrition Laboratory
courses.description: A comprehensive and applied introduction to animal nutrition with an emphasis on nutrients, digestive physiology, digestion, feed ingredient characteristics, feed identification, and ration formulation. Includes practical activities focused on developing the understanding necessary to balance appropriate diets. Corequisite(s): AVS 2101 .
courses.prerequisites: AVS major; AVS 1112 ; CHM 1210 ; CHM 1210L ; and MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , or MAT 1140 .

courses.title: Animal Genetics
courses.description: An introductory course dealing with the basic genetics of all species of livestock and common companion animals. Emphasis will be placed on inherited abnormalities, traits of economic importance, conventional methods of dealing with these traits, and technologies of the future.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1150 or BIO 1210 , BIO 1150L or BIO 1210L , and AVS major.

courses.title: Animal Industry and Society
courses.description: [GE 5D] Analysis of the application of science in the food animal industry and animal production systems, the role and use of food animals and animal products in resolving problems associated with humanity, and the influence of animal agriculture on history, civilization and human values.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Compendium
courses.description: [GE 5D] How the origins and evolution of the domestic dog and cat influence their behavior and unique nutritional requirements, how selection for desired traits leads to breed associated problems. Emergency first aid, nutrition, calculation of caloric requirements, common diseases, vaccines and the immune system, zoonotic diseases (diseases transmitted from animals to man.)
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology
courses.description: An integrated approach to the structure and function of animal systems. Topics to be discussed include the cell, the muscular-skeletal system, the nervous system, the cardiovascular system, the respiratory system, and the excretory system. Corequisite(s): AVS 3350L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1150 or BIO 1210 , BIO 1150L or BIO 1210L , CHM 1210 , CHM 1210L , and AVS major.

courses.title: Domestic Animal Anatomy Laboratory
courses.description: An integrated approach to the structure and function of animal systems. Topics to be discussed include the cell, the muscular-skeletal system, the nervous system, the cardio-vascular system, the respiratory system, and the excretory system. Corequisite(s): AVS 3350 .
courses.prerequisites: AVS major; BIO 115, BIO 1150 , BIO 121 or BIO 1210 ; BIO 115L, BIO 1150L , BIO 121L, or BIO 1210L ; CHM 121 or CHM 1210 ; and CHM 121L or CHM 1210L .

courses.title: Biotechnology Applications in Animal Science
courses.description: A study of the principles and practical applications of biotechnology in Animal Science. Discussion of the implications of genetic engineering, gene transfer, transgenic animals, embryo transfer and embryo manipulation for livestock improvement; present and future importance to the agriculture industry; human and veterinary medicine, ethical issues, patent law and strategies for future problem-solving. Appreciation of biotechniques with relevance to the Animal Sciences. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): AVS 4430LW .
courses.prerequisites: AVS 3305 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: New methods and developments, practices, and procedures in a variety of areas in the field of animal science.
courses.prerequisites: Senior Standing.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: [GE 5A] Fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including atomic and molecular structure; nomenclature; stoichiometry; solution chemistry, including acid-base and redox chemistry; quantum theory; periodic properties; bonding theory; thermochemistry; gases; and intermolecular forces. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory experiments to illustrate and enhance lecture topics in CHM 1210 . Basic laboratory techniques and practices. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210 .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: General Chemistry II
courses.description: [GE 5A] Continuation of the development of fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including kinetics; equilibria, including acid-base chemistry; buffers; titrations; thermodynamics; electrochemistry; colligative properties; and nuclear chemistry. Corequisite(s): CHM 1220L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 1210 , CHM 122 or CHM 122B; and C- or better in CHM 1210L , CHM 122L or CHM122LB.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory experiments to illustrate and enhance lecture topics in CHM 1220. Qualitative analysis. Basic laboratory techniques and practices. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 1220 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 1210 , CHM 122 or CHM 122B; and C- or better in CHM 1210L , CHM 122L or CHM122LB.

courses.title: College Algebra
courses.description: [GE 2] The theory and applications of real-valued functions, domain and range, compositions, inverses, transformations, equations and inequalities, and absolute value. Emphasis on polynomials, rational functions, power and root functions, piecewise functions, logarithms and exponential functions. Both symbolic and graphical representations of functions. Use of graphing devices to support reasoning about functions.
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, or C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: [GE 2] Functions, limits, continuity, derivatives of all functions including trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, inverse trigonometric, and implicit functions. Applications of derivatives, including max/min problems and L’Hopitals rule. Definite and Indefinite Integrals, The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, substitution rule and applications.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1050 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1052 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1055 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1070 ; AP PreCalculus >=3; or ALEKS Comp >=76.

courses.title: Statistics with Applications
courses.description: [GE 2] Sample and population data; descriptive statistics, including numerical and graphical summarization of central tendency and spread; elementary probability, including events, basic probability rules, binomial and normal distributions; inferential statistics, including confidence intervals and hypothesis tests for one-population mean and proportion problems, simple linear regression and correlation
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course, or C- or better or CR in MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Meat Science
courses.description: Introduction to processing and utilization of fresh and value-added red meat products. Discussions on identity standards, factors affecting sensory, nutritional and shelf-life quality attributes, food safety (microbiological, chemical and physical hazards), including inspection and grading of red meats.

courses.title: Animal Behavior
courses.description: The study of animal behavior including learning, cognition, behavioral physiology, biorhythms and social behavior. Emphasis will be placed on the behavior of domesticated species.
courses.prerequisites: AVS 1112 or AVS 112, AVS 1113 or AVS 113, AVS 1114L or AVS 114L, and AVS 1115L or AVS 115L.

courses.title: Mammalian Endocrinology and Physiology of Reproduction and Lactation
courses.description: Surveying the endocrine glands and their role roll in controlling development, growth, metabolism, digestion, metabolic regulation of physiological functions and the processes of reproduction from gametogenesis to parturition and galactopoiesis and lactation in domestic food producing animals. Corequisite(s): AVS 4214L .
courses.prerequisites: AVS major; AVS 350 or AVS 3350 ; and AVS 350L or AVS 3350L .

courses.title: Mammalian Reproduction and Lactational Physiology Laboratory
courses.description: A general laboratory course examining those factors which control reproductive function in domestic animals. Examine reproductive function in the female from puberty through pregnancy and parturition and from gametogenesis through puberty and gamete collection and cryopreservation in the male. 3 hour Laboratory Product fee required. Corequisite(s): AVS 4214 .
courses.prerequisites: AVS major; AVS 350 or AVS 3350 ; and AVS 350L or AVS 3350L .

courses.title: Advanced Nutrition
courses.description: Review of the advanced concepts of nutrient digestion and absorption; metabolism of proteins, carbohydrates, fats, minerals, and vitamins. Relate those concepts to applied feeding practices used in livestock production.
courses.prerequisites: AVS 101 or AVS 2101 , and AVS 2101L .

courses.title: Biology and Society
courses.description: [GE 5B] Fundamental concepts in biology are taught using socially relevant themes. Biological concepts are related to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow, exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigations, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society.

courses.title: Biology and Society Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] A laboratory support course applying lecture concepts through hands-on, inquiry-based, learn-by-doing approaches. Supports students in majors that require fundamental concepts of biology as they relate to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigation, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1110 or BIO 1150 ; BIO 1150 can be concurrent. Pre or Corequisite(s):

courses.title: Foundations of Biology: Energy, Matter, and Information
courses.description: [GE 5B] Using the central lens of evolution, this course will examine the acquisition, utilization, and flow of energy and cycling of matter through the biological hierarchy. The flow of information across different organizational levels and timescales will also be explored. Corequisite(s): BIO 1210L .

courses.title: Foundations of Biology: Energy, Matter, and Information Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Using hands-on activities, students will examine the flow of energy, the cycling of matter, and the flow of information through different timescales and organizational levels of life. Emphasis will be placed on the application of the practices of science. Corequisite(s): BIO 1210 .

courses.title: Elements of Organic Chemistry
courses.description: The fundamental concepts of organic chemistry will be presented, for students who are required to take one semester of organic chemistry. Topics covered include chemical bonding, molecular structure, stereochemistry, nomenclature, physical properties, thermodynamics and kinetics, acid-base chemistry, organic reaction mechanisms, synthesis and biomolecules. Not open to chemistry majors. Not open to chemistry majors.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; and CHM 123L or CHM 1220L .

courses.title: Elements of Organic Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to general techniques of the organic laboratory for the separation, purification and identification of organic substances. Survey of simple reactions of various functional groups. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; and CHM 123L or CHM 1220L ; or concurrent enrollment in CHM 2010 .

courses.title: Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: Modern concepts of chemical bonding, molecular structure, conformations, nomenclature, thermodynamics and kinetics, acid-base chemistry, stereochemistry, organic reaction intermediates and mechanisms, and synthesis. The physical properties, preparations and reactions of alkanes, haloalkanes, alkenes, alkynes and alcohols.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; and C- or better in CHM 123L or CHM 1220L .

courses.title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: Introduction to synthesis, isolation, purification, and characterization of organic compounds. A focus of this applied learning will be the theory, interpretation, and application of identifying compounds utilizing IR and NMR spectra. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 3140 or CHM 315; CHM 3140 can be concurrent.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Undergraduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
